sources: installer-builder-runtimes catalog/java/releases.json and gaps.json (own scrape of Adoptium + Zulu APIs, used as ground truth for which OS/arch builds currently exist per major)

milestones.notes: JEP-less era; generics, enhanced for, autoboxing, enums, varargs, annotations all landed together in J2SE 5.0
lambda expressions, method references, functional interfaces, default/static interface methods
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture; streams API shipped the same release
java.nio.file (Path/Files/WatchService) plus true async channels (AsynchronousSocketChannel/AsynchronousFileChannel); 1.4's original java.nio was non-blocking but not asynchronous
implemented in JSSE from 7 but not enabled by default; became a default-enabled protocol in 8
JEP 332; backported to Oracle/OpenJDK 8 in update 8u261 (2020)
java.net.http.HttpClient standardized (incubated in 9); HTTP/2 and WebSocket support
JEP 517, preview only as of 26; HttpClient gains HTTP/3
Java Platform Module System / Project Jigsaw, JEP 261
local-variable type inference, JEP 286; extended to lambda params in 11
standardized JEP 395; previewed in 14 and 15
standardized JEP 409; previewed in 15 and 16
pattern matching for switch standardized (JEP 441); pattern matching for instanceof standardized earlier, in 16
standardized JEP 444; previewed in 19 and 20; carrier-thread pinning inside synchronized blocks not fixed until 24 (JEP 491)
first previewed as an incubator in 19 (JEP 428); still only preview as of 26 (sixth preview, JEP 525) — not yet finalized (targeted for 28)
standardized JEP 392 (native per-OS installers/app-images); incubated in 14 (JEP 343)
Windows/AArch64 port, JEP 388; vendor build availability has been inconsistent release-to-release since (present in Temurin/Zulu for some non-LTS majors, absent for others)

macOS/AArch64 port, JEP 391 — first native Apple Silicon OpenJDK; earlier majors run under Rosetta 2 only, except that Azul Zulu separately ships a native Apple Silicon build of 8 for legacy compatibility
Linux/AArch64 available from vendor builds (e.g. Zulu) as far back as 8, ahead of it being a mainline OpenJDK port target; coverage has been inconsistent for some interim (non-LTS) majors
Sun shipped an official 64-bit Windows (x64) build within the 5.0 update train (~2007); this catalog's own release data only goes back to major 6
dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 socket support
Solaris JDK switched from cooperative green threads to native OS threads in 1.2; Windows/Win32 builds used native threads from 1.0
follows native_threads — Java never had a global interpreter lock, so true multi-core parallelism was available once native threading landed
UTF-8 made the default charset everywhere (JEP 400), removing platform-default-encoding surprises; internal String/char representation has been UTF-16 since 1.0

os_support.macos: none from Sun; Apple shipped its own Mac OS Runtime for Java (MRJ), a separate implementation
os_support.linux: none official; unofficial ports followed later (Blackdown project)

added: core language: classes, interfaces, exceptions, single inheritance
cooperative green threads on Solaris (Win32 used native OS threads from the start)
limitations: no inner classes (1.1)
no collections framework — only Vector/Hashtable (1.2)
no Swing (1.2)
no generics — raw Object and casts everywhere (5)
green threads on Solaris meant no true multi-core parallelism there until 1.2

os_support.windows: Windows 95/98/NT 4.0 (32-bit)
os_support.macos: none from Sun; Apple's MRJ tracked 1.1 separately for Mac OS Classic
os_support.linux: none official; Blackdown ported 1.1 unofficially

limitations: no collections framework or Swing (1.2)
no generics or autoboxing (5)
no strictfp (1.2)
no JIT bundled by default (HotSpot arrives 1.3)

os_support.windows: Windows 95/98/NT 4.0
os_support.macos: none from Sun in this line; Apple's MRJ 2.x tracked 1.1.x APIs rather than a full 1.2
os_support.linux: Blackdown ported 1.2 unofficially; no Sun-official Linux build yet

added: switch from cooperative green threads to native OS threads on Solaris
limitations: no HotSpot JVM by default yet (1.3)
no generics — collections hold Object and need casts (5)
no regex, NIO, or assert keyword (1.4)
still 32-bit only

os_support.macos: none from Sun; Apple shipped 1.3 support in Mac OS X 10.0/10.1 as its own build
os_support.linux: Sun began official Linux (x86) builds around this line, alongside continuing unofficial Blackdown ports

limitations: no assert keyword or NIO (1.4)
no regex or logging API (1.4)

added: java.nio (buffers, channels, selectors) — non-blocking I/O, but not yet asynchronous I/O (that's NIO.2, 7)
JAXP (XML) and Java Web Start bundled
limitations: no generics — raw types and casts everywhere (5)
no enhanced for-loop, autoboxing, enums, varargs, or annotations (5)

os_support.windows: Windows 98/Me/NT4/2000/XP; an official 64-bit (x64) Windows build arrived via a later 5.0 update
os_support.macos: Apple shipped Java 5 for Mac OS X 10.4 Tiger (PowerPC and Intel) as its own build — the last Java Apple shipped for PowerPC Macs
os_support.linux: Sun-official x86 and x86_64 builds

limitations: no closures/lambdas — anonymous inner classes are the only option (8)
no try-with-resources or diamond operator (7)
no switch on String (7)
generics are erased at runtime and don't cover primitives directly
no module system — flat classpath only (9)

os_support.windows: Windows 2000/XP/Server 2003/Vista, with later updates adding Windows 7/8; current Adoptium/Zulu rebuilds of this major provide amd64 only, though Sun originally also shipped 32-bit x86
os_support.macos: Apple shipped Java 6 for Mac OS X 10.5/10.6 as its own build (32- and 64-bit Intel; PowerPC dropped) — the last Java version Apple bundled directly into the OS. No third-party (Adoptium/Zulu) macOS rebuild of major 6 exists today
os_support.linux: Sun/Oracle-official x86 and x86_64; current catalog rebuilds (Temurin/Zulu) provide linux/amd64 only, no arm

limitations: no lambdas, streams, or default interface methods (8)
no module system (9)
no try-with-resources or diamond operator (7)
no fork/join framework (7)
Oracle didn't take over Mac maintenance from Apple until partway through this major's life

os_support.windows: Windows XP SP3/Vista/7/8, 32-bit and 64-bit — the last major with routine 32-bit Windows client support before it thinned out industry-wide
os_support.macos: first release Oracle (not Apple) distributed directly, for OS X 10.7.3 Lion and later, x86_64 only; no arm64 (Apple Silicon didn't exist yet)
os_support.linux: x86, x86_64; ARM (armv7/armhf) support existed via separate Oracle/OpenJDK embedded builds, not the mainstream desktop ones

added: NIO.2 (java.nio.file: Path/Files/WatchService) with true asynchronous channels
binary literals and underscores in numeric literals
limitations: no lambdas or streams — verbose anonymous classes for callbacks (8)
TLS 1.1/1.2 implemented in JSSE but not enabled by default (default-enabled in 8)
no module system (9)
no java.time — still java.util.Date/Calendar (8)
no var inference (10)

majors.end_of_life: 2030-12 (Oracle Extended Support); Premier ended 2022-03; free public updates for personal use ended 2019-01

os_support.windows: Windows Vista SP2/7/8/8.1/10, amd64 and x86; XP dropped. No arm64 build (that port didn't exist until 16, and was never backported here)
os_support.macos: OS X 10.7.3 Lion and later, x86_64. No native Apple Silicon build from Oracle for this line — Rosetta 2 is required on M-series Macs; Azul Zulu separately ships a native Apple Silicon (arm64) build of 8, added long after 2014, purely for legacy-app compatibility
os_support.linux: x86, x86_64, arm64, and armv7

added: TLS 1.2 enabled by default for client connections
limitations: no module system — classpath conflicts persist (9)
no var (10)
no records, sealed types, or pattern matching (14-21)
no virtual threads — thread-per-request stays expensive (21)
no built-in HTTP/2 client (11)
32-bit Windows/Linux builds still routine here; this is roughly the last major where that's true across most vendors

os_support.windows: Windows 7/8/8.1/10, amd64 and x86 (Oracle's own 32-bit Windows JDK builds ended around this release). No arm64 build
os_support.macos: OS X 10.10+, x86_64 only
os_support.linux: x86, x86_64 only — no arm64 or armv7 builds available in mainstream OpenJDK redistributions for this specific major

added: Java Platform Module System / Project Jigsaw (JEP 261)

Oracle's own 32-bit Windows JDK builds end around this release
no var (10)

os_support.windows: Windows 7 SP1/8.1/10, amd64 and x86; no arm64 build for this major
